Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2647; indissoluble, i.e. (figuratively) permanent:--endless.
BiblicalUsage: Once, of the priesthood of Christ: He is made a priest not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life. The word is indissoluble — a life that cannot be broken apart, a priesthood that cannot end because the Priest cannot die.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for an endless life carries little weight on its own; its weight is the verse, a Priest who cannot die and therefore saves to the uttermost.
RelatedTopics: Priesthood; Eternal Life; Superiority of Christ
